replacement.briefing: F1 controls below the attacking goal line. F2 has moved down the side boards to support. YOU are arriving from the high slot. The exercise calls for one forward to remain higher than the puck as an outlet. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: Both F1 and F2 have greater x positions, deeper toward the attacking end.

sources.title: U15 / U18 Core Skills — Train to Train
sources.section: Page 1, Team Play / Offensive Skills: cycling and support
sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

replacement.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Which two forwards are already deeper in Gold’s end than YOU?

options.text: F1 and F2
D1 and D2
Gold 1 and Gold 3

questions.explanation: Both F1 and F2 have greater x positions, deeper toward the attacking end.

questions.prompt: Which two checks help retain a high outlet?

options.text: Whether every forward should follow the puck low
F1’s ability to see out of pressure
Gold 2’s position in the middle

questions.explanation: The assigned high role creates another option but still needs a lane.

questions.prompt: Arrange a high-support read during this cycle.

options.text: Notice F2 joining low
Check the open high-slot pocket
Reoffer high support behind the puck

questions.explanation: The exercise defines the high role; actual timing should follow the carrier’s pressure.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot pocket separated from the two low forwards.
questions.explanation: The reference changes the lane around Gold 2 without joining the low cluster. Another high pocket may work.

questions.prompt: If F1 passes to YOU in that pocket, what should happen next?

options.text: Return the puck low without looking
Read the new pressure before choosing shot, pass or carry
Shoot automatically because YOU are high

questions.explanation: The support movement creates a new decision rather than a predetermined finish.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between the high slot and following F2 down the half wall.
questions.explanation: Use depth, passing angle and the team’s remaining support—not just the two area names.

questions.prompt: What should YOU call while F2 cycles below?

options.text: I am high; show me if F1 can use the outlet
The low cycle makes the high lane irrelevant
F1 is the preferred receiver even if the high lane closes

questions.explanation: The call preserves a high option while the low carrier changes.

questions.prompt: Which two cues support staying high?

options.text: F1 and F2 occupy different low spaces
The carrier can see a high outlet
The distance to the boards decides whether to stay high

questions.explanation: Separation and visibility explain the high support choice.

questions.prompt: F1 cycles the puck down to F2 below the goal line. Move YOU to a new high-slot pocket that keeps a passing lane open from F2.
questions.explanation: This point adjusts the angle to F2's new puck touch instead of F1's original spot, while staying clear of the low forwards. Another high pocket may also keep the lane open.

questions.prompt: F1 passes to YOU in the pocket. What should be scanned next?
questions.explanation: Check Gold coverage, F2's route, and the net-side lane before choosing a shot, pass, or reset.

reasons.issue: Lowercase "you" in option (c), "Shoot automatically because you are high."
reasons.change: Changed option (c) text to "Shoot automatically because YOU are high." Answer key (b) and all other fields unchanged.
reasons.evidence: Same mandatory-style rule as above; house style requires all-caps YOU everywhere, including inside distractor options.

reasons.issue: Option (c), "YOU is closest to the boards," has a subject-verb agreement error and is also geometrically false: recomputed distance-to-boards for each home skater (boards at y=+-12.954) shows YOU (y=0) is 12.95m from the boards, the farthest of the five home skaters, not the closest (F2 at y=-9 is 3.95m away).
reasons.change: Replaced option (c) text with "The distance to the boards decides whether to stay high," removing both the grammar error and the false positional claim while keeping a plausible-but-insufficient cue as the wrong answer. Answer key (a,b) unchanged.
reasons.evidence: Computed sqrt-distance from each home actor y-coordinate to y=+-12.954 directly from setup.actors in the scenario.

reasons.issue: q9's prompt duplicated q4's prompt almost verbatim ("Move YOU into a high-slot pocket separated from the low forwards" vs. "...separated from the two low forwards"), differing only by a reference-point shift, with no new cue or decision -- the sibling-duplication defect class from packet-31's lesson 9.
reasons.change: Changed q9's prompt to introduce an explicit hypothetical ("F1 cycles the puck down to F2 below the goal line. Move YOU to a new high-slot pocket that keeps a passing lane open from F2."), moved the reference point to (14,3) (~15m from both F1 and F2, ~3.6m from D1, confirmed on ice), and rewrote the explanation to justify the new angle relative to F2's puck touch instead of restating q4's static read.
reasons.evidence: Prompt-string comparison against q4, and recomputed distances from the new reference (14,3) to F1 (28,-4), F2 (23,-9) and D1 (11,5).

sourceChecks.scope: Single-page U15/U18 'LTPD Stage - Train to Train' skills matrix (titled internally 'Draft 2017 - Bantam - Midget Pathway'). Team Play/Defensive Skills lists 'Timing And Support - Spatial Awareness', 'Situational Gap Control', 'Read and React' and 'Communication'; Team Play/Offensive Skills lists 'Cycling', 'Smart Puck Support Principles (Under Pressure)', 'Entries', 'Retrievals', 'Hinging', 'Delays' and 'Net Drives'. It names these as topic labels for the age band; it contains no coordinates, coaching scripts, guaranteed outcomes or the specific coverage-communication/cycle-support wording used in exp26-u15-008 or exp26-u15-009. Supports age/topic placement only, exactly as sources.json's own use field discloses; does not certify the setup, alternatives or suggested answers.
